title: Permission fuzz harness + deterministic fixture library for RBAC v2 regression
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: RBAC v2 expands role composition, attribute-based mappings (SAML/SCIM), and admin-only controls. We lack a single deterministic test harness that combines randomized permission fuzzing with reproducible scenario fixtures and audit-log correlation checks. Goal: deliver a permission-fuzz harness plus a deterministic fixture library and CI-integrated regression suite that validates both allow/deny semantics and that audit logs capture the correct decision metadata for every evaluated request. This reduces regression risk for RBAC policy changes, role rollouts, and SSO mapping updates.

Scope: build a harness that can run in two modes: (1) fuzz mode to explore edge-case combinations of permissions, roles, resource descriptors, and SAML attributes; (2) replay mode that executes deterministic fixtures (scenario templates) to verify historical regressions and guardrails. Integrate with existing audit log ingestion test endpoint and produce human-readable trace artifacts for triage. Provide a fixture builder CLI and JSON fixture catalog to be checked into tests/rbac-fixtures/ in repo.

Non-goals: not replacing production policy engines; not covering exhaustive performance benchmarking (separate perf project).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run in fuzz and replay mode via make test-rbac-harness
Deterministic fixtures are stored under repo path tests/rbac-fixtures/ and include at least 30 varied scenarios (admin, ops, delegated, service-account, cross-tenant, SAML role mapping edgecases)
For each fixture, the suite asserts decision (allow/deny), reason codes, and that audit-log events contain expected fields (request_id, principal_id, role_snapshot, policy_version)
CI job rbac-regressions runs on PRs touching rbac/ or auth/ and fails on any semantic drift
Test artifacts (request traces and sanitized audit payloads) are uploaded to the artifacts bucket for failed runs and linked in the Linear ticket
test_plan: Create fixture schema v1 with fields: scenario_id, principal, roles, attributes, resource, action, expected_decision, expected_audit_fields
Implement harness engine that seeds a synthetic principal store and can optionally hit a local auth sandbox or stubbed policy evaluator
Implement audit stub that records decision events to a test ingestion topic and exposes an HTTP endpoint for assertions
Author initial 30 fixtures covering RBAC v2 capabilities and SAML attribute-to-role mapping edgecases
Add CI GH workflow job .github/workflows/rbac-regression.yml to run harness in replay mode and upload artifacts
implementation_notes: Use Python harness (pytest plugin) to leverage parametrized fixtures and hypothesis for fuzz mode
Fixture schema must be JSON Schema compatible to allow validation in CI
When running fuzz mode, save the seed and shrinker path to allow deterministic replays of any discovered failure
Correlate policy decisions with audit events by propagating X-Test-Run-Id and matching on the ingestion side
Sanitize PHI/PII from audit payloads before storing artifacts (use redact-audit util)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fuzzing may produce nondeterministic failures. Mitigation: always persist seed and environment snapshot so failures are replayable.

Risk: Test harness may diverge from production policy evaluation. Mitigation: provide a 'production-compat' stub that mirrors the production evaluator's plugin interfaces and include a smoke test against a dedicated staging evaluator.
Risk: Audit ingestion test doubles may omit fields present in production. Mitigation: copy production audit schema and run schema validation as part of build.
Risk: SAML attribute variability across IdPs might cause brittle fixtures. Mitigation: model attribute sets and provide mapping templates (okta, azure, google) in fixtures catalog.
